Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 12pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be summarized
by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City Council and will
also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be recorded for
public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

2. Consideration of an Ordinance to Amend a Zoning Code and an Appeal of the

Consumption

Following the conclusion of the Public Hearing, it is recommended that the City Council:
(CD)

a. Determine that the proposed text amendment is exempt from further review under the
California Environmental Quality Act (California Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et

Regulations §§ 15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”), because it consists of only minor
text revisions and clarifications to existing zoning regulations and procedures related

findings required. Therefore, in accordance with CEQA, the proposed text amendment is
exempt from CEQA pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) because the activity is governed by

significant effect on the environment. In this case, the proposed text amendment will not

(CEQA), the request for approval of a Conditional Use Permit (“CUP”) qualifies for a
categorical exemption under CEQA Guidelines Section 15301, (Class 1) “Existing

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials

During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items

Agenda Items 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 are Consent Calendar Items. All items including Ordinances,
Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent Calendar,
individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion of these
items unless Members of the City Council, the public, or staff request that specific items be
removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members of the
public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three (3)
minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

  6
 MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  AUTHORIZING  THE APPLICATION  FOR CALIFORNIA
GOVERNOR'S  OFFICE  OF EMERGENCY  SERVICES  ("CAL OES") GRANT FtJNDS
FOR THE EMERGNECY  OPERATION  CENTER ("EOC")  PROJECT,  CITY PROJECT
N0. 582-ARC

PURPOSE:  Approval  of the Resolution  will authorize the submittal of an application for
grant funding  to the California Governor's  Office Of Emergency Services ("Cal OES") for the
Emergen7onCenter("EOC")Project  ("Project").

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will consider:
  a. Adopting a Resolution authorizing the application for the California Govemor's Office
  Of Emergency Services, requesting  $1,226,000 in grant funds, for the Emergency
  Operations Center, City Project No. 582-ARC; and
  b.  Authorizing  the City Manager, or his designee, to execute, on behalf  of the City,  all
  documents  requiredto submit the application aiimplementthe  grant.

FISCAL IMPACT:  There is no impact to the General Fund. The grant application requests
$1,226,000 to fund the Project, however, it also includes a $408,667 commitment in matching
funds for a total project budget of $1,634,667.  Staff is reviewing funding options for the
matching funds thus as of the date of this Council Meeting a fiinding source(s)  has not been
selected.

ANALYSIS:  Cal OES has allocated $1,226,000 in grant funds to fund the construction of a new
EOC within the City Hall grounds. To secure the grant 'funds, the Cal OES requires a Resolution
from the City Council authorizing the application and use of the funds. Key points of the
required Resolution  include:

  The Resolution authorizes the submission of an application to apply for the Cal OES
  grant in the amount of $1,226,000 and commits to a local match requirement of
  $408,667, for a total budget of $ 1,634,667.

  *  The City certifies  that sufficient  funds will  be available  to complete  and maintain  the
  project.

  l

  104
   *  The  City  Manager,  or  his  designee,  is  authorized  to  handle  all  project-related
  negotiations,  including  agreements  and payment  requests.

BACKGROUND:  The  South  Gate  Police  Station,  built  in  1948,  houses  an Emergency
Operations  Center  ("EOC")  in a subterranean  section  of the building.  This  location  is prone  to
flooding,  lacks  ADA-compliant  access,  and faces significant  communication  challenges  due to
the thick  concrete  walls.  Given  that effective  communication  is critical  for emergency  response,
staff recommends  relocating  the EOC to ensure reliable  operations  during  major  events.

The project  relocates  the existing  EOC  from  the SGPD  basement  to a new facility  at the Civic
Center  by repurposing  a portion  of the museum  to meet modern  EOC  requirements.  The section
of  the  museum  is planned  to  serve  a dual  purpose:  an as-needed  EOC  and  a Community
room/Museum.  Daily,  the improved  section  will  serve  for  conference  room,  community  room
and a Museum.  However,  when  the EOC  is activated,  that will  be shut down  to the public  and
the EOC will  be activated.

Some of the displays  in this portion  of the museum  that will  be improved  will  be relocated  to the
easterly  side of the museum  section.  They  will  continue  to be available  for public  viewing  to the
extent  practical.  Other  displays  will  be integrated  into  the room  keeping  part  of the Museum
experience  while  still  allotting  appropriate  space for the EOC needs.

As  a note,  the  originally  proposed  relocation  was  to  8640  California  Avenue  (South  Gate
Courthouse).  However,  that  presented  significant  challenges,  including  asbestos  removal,
seismic  retrofitting  to comply  with  the 2024  Building  Code,  and insufficient  staff  parking.  The
Civic  Center  location  avoids  these issues, making  it a more suitable  choice  for the new EOC.

The proposed  budget  is $1,634,667.  Work  includes,  but is not limited  to, upgrading  electrical  and
mechanical  systems  for proper  heating  and air conditioning,  a backup  generator,  equipping  the
space with  televisions,  tables,  computers,  desks,  radios,  and cell  phones  to support  emergency
operations.  The proposed  budget  will  be expended  as summarized  below.

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH  OSCAR'S  ELECTRIC,  INC.,  FOR  THE
INST ALLATION  OF THREE  LEVEL  2 ELECTRIC  VEHICLE  CHARGING  ST ATIONS
AT  CITY  HALL

PURPOSE:  To award  an agreement  to Oscar's  Electric,  Inc., for the installation  of three Level
2 Electric  Vehicle  Charging  Stations  in the City Hall's  underground  parking  garage.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  an Agreement  with  Oscar's  Electric,  Inc.,  for the installation  of three Level  2
  Electric  Vehicle  Charging  Stations  in the City  Hall's  underground  parking  garage,  in an
  amount  not-to-exceed  $25,843;
  b.  Appropriating  $35,000  from  the AQMD  Fund  Balance  to fully  fund  the purchase  and
  installation  of the Level  2 Electric  Vehicle  Charging  Stations;  and
  c.  Authorizing  the  Mayor  to  execute  the  Agreement  in  a form  acceptable  to the  City
  Attorney.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact  to the General  Fund.  The proposed  Agreement
with  Oscar  Electric,  Inc.,  will  be funded  with  $25,843  in South  Coast Air  Quality  Management
District  ("AQMD")  Funds.  The recomi'nended  appropriation  is $35,000  from  the AQMD  Fund
Balance.

ANALYSIS:  One of the City  of South  Gate's  ("City")  initiatives  is to purchase  electric  vehicles
("EVs")  as part  of its corni'nitment  to environmental  protection.  This  effort  also requires  the
installation  of Electric  Vehicle  Charging  Stations  ("EVCS").  The City's  vision  is to install  Level
2 EVCS  in City  Hall's  underground  parking  garage.  To date, three charging  stations  have been
installed,  leaving  a need for three more.

Staff  recommends  awarding  a sole-source  agreement  to  Oscar's  Electric  in  the  amount  of
$25,843  to  install  the  additional  EVCS.  Oscar's  Electric  has the  necessary  experience  and
expertise,  having  recently  installed  a Level  2 charging  station  and upgraded  an existing  one in
City  Hall's  underground  garage.  They  also conducted  power  monitoring,  giving  them a thorough
understanding  of the building's  electrical  equipment  and supply.  Given  their  familiarity  with  the
system,  they  are well-positioned  to install  the new charging  stations  and complete  the required
electrical  upgrades  in a cost-effective  manner.

 While  the  proposed  contract  amount  is $25,843,  tlie  total  project  budget  is $35,000.  This
includes  $5,157  in contingency  funds and $4,000  to purchase  three EVCS  units.

BACKGROUND:  This  initiative  seeks  to  improve  the  City's  electric  vehicle  ("EV")
infrastructure  by  installing  three  Level  2 EV  charging  stations  in the underground  parking
garage  at  City  Hall.  These  enhancements  align  with  the  City's  sustainability  goals  and
commitment  to  expanding  EV  accessibility  for  employees  and  visitors.  By  addressing  the
growing  demand  for  EV  charging,  this  project  will  contribute  to  a more  sustainable  and
environmentally  friendly  community.
The scope of work  includes:

  Installation  of a 3-Phase transfon'ner  to support  the additional  electrical  load.

  *  Installation  of a 225 Amp,  120/208V  3-Phase panel to distribute  power  efficiently.

  *  Installation  of three City-provided  Level  2 charging  stations.

Staff  recommends  awarding  a $25,843  contract  to Oscar's  Electric,  Inc.,  a Santa  Fe Springs-
based  contractor  with  over  30 years  of  experience  in  electrical  infrastructure  projects.  The
company  previously  installed  and  upgraded  EV  charging  stations  at City  Hall  and  has  a
thorough  understanding  of the site's  electrical  system,  ensuring  a cost-effective  and seamless
installation.

Construction  is scheduled  to begin  in March  2025,  with  an expected  completion  time  of I to 2
weeks.

The total  project  budget  is $35,000, which  includes  contingency  funds  and the purchase  of the
three charging  stations.

which  totaled  $381,342  and released  within  60 days of completion  of the work.  Construction  will
be  completed  on  February  21,  2025;  thus,  the  retention  payment  is  due  April  21,  2025.
However,  tlie  Public  Works  Department  plans  to authorize  release  of  50%  of the  retention
amount  after  City  Council  approval  of the NOC  and then release tlie balance  on Apiil  21, 2025.
This  is justified  because  SCE is taking  longer  than  expected  to schedule  crews  to energize  a

service  pedestal  that was installed  on the Project.  SCE plans  to energize  it in March  2025.  This
creates  a schedule  extension  that  is beyond  the  contractor's  control.  Further,  the  schedule
extension  does not impact  the status of work  already  completed  by the contractor  for wl'iich  liens
could be filed.  Withholding  50% retention  would  suffice  in meeting  contract  obligations.

BACKGROUND:  This project  is part of the Capital  Improvement  Program,  aimed  at enhancing
safety,  traffic  circulation,  landscaping,  greening,  and beautification  along Long  Beach  Boulevard
from  Santa  Ana  Street  to Tweedy  Boulevard.  Using  a complete  streets  approach,  the project
improves  conditions  for vehicles,  bicycles,  and pedestrians  while  supporting  energy  efficiency
and alternative  transportation.

On May  23, 2023, the City  Council  approved  Contract  No. 2023-67-CC  with  Sequel  Contractors,
Inc., for $7,578,763.  Construction  began  September  11, 2023, and concluded  February  21, 2025.

Two  change  orders  were  necessary  to complete  construction  and approved  administratively,  as
follows:

  *  On February  10, 2025,  Change  Order  No. 1 was administratively  approved  in the amount
  of  $408,071.  Improvements  included  unforeseen  electrical  work,  curb  ramps,  median
  island,  solar-powered  irrigation  system,  relocation  of pedestrian  lighting,  and  traffic
  safety  improvements.

  *  On Febmary  18, 2025, Change  Order  No. 2 was administratively  approved,  resulting  in a
  $360,000  cost reduction  in the contract  amount.  This  reflects  a $517,361 deduction  for
  work  that  was  not  needed  to  complete  construction.  It  also  reflects  $157,361  for
  additional  improvements  completed,  work  sucli  as expanded  pavement  removal  and
  replacement,  increased  median  and parkway  topsoil  application,  additional  concrete  work
  for  parkway  bioswale  installation,  additional  traffic  pushbutton  installations  and
  pedestrian  lighting.

The final  contract  amount  was $7,626,833.

The contractor  has fulfilled  all contract  obligations,  completing  the work  in accordance  with
approved  plans  and specifications  while  maintaining  quality  cra'ftsmanship,  staying  within
budget,  and meeting  the project  timeline.  The project  completed  has been inspected  and
confirmed  to meet all required  standards.

  Representative

  del Pilar  Avalos,  Council  Member  Gil  Hurtado  and Council  Member  Al
  Rios;  City  Treasurer  Jose De La Paz, City  Manager  Rob  Houston,  City
  Attorney  Raul  F. Salinas

GUEST  SPEAKER  Hector  De La Torre  stated  that the Gateway  Cities  of Council  of
  Governments  is an association  of twenty-seven  cities,  eleven
  unincorporated  areas from  East LA  to Long  Beach.  From  here to Orange
  County  boarder.  This  association  does things  collaboratively  that  spill  over
  city  lines,  transportation,  housing  and homelessness,  environment,
  economic  development,  and health  & wellness.

  the City  Council:

  a.  Determine  that  the proposed  text  amendment  is exempt  from
  further  review  under  the California  Environmental  Quality  Act
  (California  Public  Resources  Code  §§ 21000,  et seq., "CEQA")
  and the regulations  promulgated  there  under  (14 California  Code
  of Regulations  §§ 15000,  et seq., the "CEQA  Guidelines"),
  because  it consists  of only  minor  text  revisions  and clarifications  to
  existing  zoning  regulations  and procedures  related  thereto,  and will
  not have  the effect  of substantially  changing  regulatory  standards
  or findings  required.  Therefore,  in accordance  with  CEQA,  the
  proposed  text amendment  is exempt  from  CEQA  pursuant  to
  Section  15061(b)(3)  because  the activity  is governed  by the

PERMITS  CONT'D  general  rule that CEQA  applies  only to projects  that have the
  potential  to cause a significant  effect  on the environment.  In this
  case, the proposed  text amendment  will  not have a significant
  effect  on the environment.

  Furthermore,  determine  that in accordance  with  the California
  Environmental  Quality  Act  (CEQA),  the request  for approval  of a
  Conditional  Use Permit  ("CUP")  qualifies  for a categorical
  exemption  under  CEQA  Guidelines  Section  15301,  (Class 1)
  "Existing  Facilities",  in that the project  will  not result  in any
  alterations  or expansion  to the existing  buildings  within  the project
  site.

  Introduce  an Ordinance,  waive  further  reading  and read by title
  only:
  AN  ORDINANCE  AMENDING  CHAPTER  11.21  (LAND  USE
  TYPES)  OF TITLE  11 (ZONING)  OF THE  SOUTH  GATE
  MUNICIPAL  CODE  (SGMC),  RELATING  TO RESTAURANTS
  AND  ANCILLARY  ALCOHOL  SALES  WITHIN  ALL  OPEN
  SPACE  (OS) ZONING  DISTRICTS  IN THE  CITY.

  Uphold  the action  taken by the Planning  Commission  at its
  December  5, 2024,  meeting,  by adopting  a Resolution  attached
  hereto  (Attachment  A), approving  a Conditional  Use Permit  (CUP
  24-15)  to allow  the sales of alcohol  (ABC  License  Type 41 - beer
  and wine)  for on-site  consumption  in conjunction  with  an existing
  restaurant/cat6  located  within  a soccer facility  at 9599 Pinehurst
  Avenue  (the "SoFive  Soccer  Complex").
